correctness.rationale: For every E>0, the time-preserving map q=-log(1-x), p=-y gives the coercive convex energy H=p²/2+q+exp(-q)-1. The exact positive-side energy-gap identity w-exp(-a)(exp(w)-1), together with monotonicity of (exp(w)-1)/w, bounds all positive passage times uniformly. The negative side is O((log E)/sqrt E) by splitting at w=1. Hence Q_E converges uniformly to the specified parabola and P_E converges in L1 to a sawtooth. The identity x ds=-(sqrt(2E)/T)dP_E, L1 momentum convergence, and uniformly bounded signed-measure total variation establish x ds -> ds-delta_{1/2} against all continuous tests. Two inverse branches establish the normalized occupation density. Critical boundary E->infinity and phase origin at q-positive turning are explicit. No finite experiment substitutes for the limit proof.

originality.rationale: Relevant 2022 Loud-family period-criticality manuscript, 2007 exact undamped Toda oscillator paper, 2005 Loud period-function paper, and 2021 singular exponential oscillators article were compared at statement and implication level. Prior known period scaling and energy quadrature are credited. The 2007 paper approximates time waveforms but does not establish an exact distributional signed-force impulse with total-variation control and universal time-sampling law. No covering result found in examined results; general singular-impact analogues remain a documented priority risk.
residual_risks: 2007 Toda paper already provides a full energy quadrature and accurate large-amplitude profile fits; a rigorously proved equivalent limit under a transformed observable may be present in other physical-oscillator literature.
Searches of a finite set of sources and published indexed records do not establish absolute novelty; some complete source sections not about phase measures were not read line-by-line.
The formal signed-impulse limit is only for one conserved undamped parameter and one prescribed phase origin; finite-amplitude quantitative estimates are not supplied.

value.rationale: The signed pulse amplitude concentrates precisely enough to survive as a negative point mass despite almost-everywhere convergence of the observable to +1; this is a nontrivial structural law, not a negligible finite-energy correction. Its exact mass is locked by the physical-time conservation coboundary, while the universal continuous-time phase and energy-share distribution distinguish this high-energy regime from a smooth oscillator. It directly quantifies a natural physically measured force for a classical integrable oscillator and can organize tests of damping or phase observables; no paper-sized downstream theorem is claimed.
